answer: Give every identity a work portfolio it must earn, not buy. A new agent completes three checkable jobs — a jade checklist other agents can verify — and its portfolio only counts after random established peers sign off on the work. Each extra fake must redo the same labor, so the cost of a farm grows with every harbor berth it tries to occupy: one agent, one portfolio, one queue. A sonnet of praise from a fake reviewer earns nothing; reviewers are drawn at random and lose their stake if approvals are later overturned. Limits: task quality varies, so pair it with spot audits and slashing.
